title.en: Volume 162 Biographies 112: Pan Mengyang, Li Shu, Wang Sui, Cao Hua, Wei Shou, Zheng Quan, Lu Shimei, Han Quanyi, Gao Xiayi, Gao Yu, Cui Rong, Lu Gen, Zhang Zhengfu

sentences.zh: 潘孟陽，禮部侍郎炎之子也。

translations.literal: Pan Mengyang was the son of Yan, Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Mengyang was the son of Yan, Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 孟陽以父廕進，登博學宏辭科。

translations.literal: Mengyang advanced through his father's yin privilege and passed the Broad Learning and Eloquent Expression examination.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang entered service through his father's privilege and passed the Boxue Hongci examination.

sentences.zh: 累遷殿中侍御史，降為司議郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Palace Censor, then demoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Palace Censor, then was demoted to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 孟陽母，劉晏女也。

translations.literal: Mengyang's mother was a daughter of Liu Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang's mother was Liu Yan's daughter.

sentences.zh: 公卿多父友及外祖賓從，故得薦用，累至兵部郎中。

translations.literal: Many ministers and officials were his father's friends and his maternal grandfather's associates and followers, so he was recommended for appointment and rose to Bureau Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Many high officials were friends of his father or associates of his maternal grandfather, so he won recommendations and rose to bureau director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 德宗末，王紹以恩幸，數稱孟陽之材，因擢授權知戶部侍郎，年未四十。

translations.literal: Late in Dezong's reign, Wang Shao, favored for his intimacy with the emperor, repeatedly praised Mengyang's talent, and Mengyang was therefore promoted to Acting Vice Minister of Revenue before the age of forty.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Dezong's reign, Wang Shao, a favorite of the emperor, often praised Mengyang's ability, and Mengyang was made acting vice minister of revenue while still under forty.

sentences.zh: 順宗即位，永貞內禪，王叔文誅，杜佑始專判度支，請孟陽代叔文為副。

translations.literal: When Shunzong took the throne after the Yongzhen inner succession, Wang Shuwen was executed, and Du You began to oversee the Bureau of Public Revenue alone; he asked that Mengyang replace Shuwen as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: After Shunzong's accession and the Yongzhen abdication, with Wang Shuwen dead, Du You took sole charge of the revenue bureau and asked that Mengyang replace Shuwen as deputy.

sentences.zh: 時憲宗新即位，乃命孟陽巡江淮省財賦，仍加鹽鐵轉運副使，且察東南鎮之政理。

translations.literal: The emperor, newly enthroned, then ordered Mengyang to tour the Jianghuai region to inspect finances, and also made him deputy salt and iron transport commissioner, with authority to examine governance in the southeastern commands.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong, newly enthroned, sent Mengyang to tour Jianghuai and inspect revenues, also appointing him deputy salt-and-iron transport commissioner to review governance in the southeastern commands.

sentences.zh: 時孟陽以氣豪權重，領行從三四百人，所歷鎮府，但務遊賞，與婦女為夜飲。

translations.literal: At the time Mengyang, arrogant and wielding great power, led a retinue of three or four hundred men; in every command he passed through he devoted himself only to pleasure outings and nightly drinking with women.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang traveled with three or four hundred attendants, and in every command he visited he did nothing but carouse and drink through the night with women.

sentences.zh: 至鹽鐵轉運院，廣納財賄，補吏職而已。

translations.literal: At the salt and iron transport office he broadly accepted bribes and merely filled official posts.
translations.idiomatic: At the transport office he took bribes on a wide scale and did little beyond filling posts.

sentences.zh: 及歸，大失人望，罷為大理卿。

translations.literal: When he returned, he had lost the people's esteem and was dismissed to serve as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he had lost all public esteem and was removed to serve as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 三年，出為華州刺史，遷梓州刺史、劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was sent out as governor of Hua Prefecture, then transferred to governor of Zi Prefecture and military governor of Eastern Chuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became governor of Hua, then of Zi, and military governor of Eastern Chuan.

sentences.zh: 與武元衡有舊，元衡作相，復召為戶部侍郎、判度支，兼京北五城營田使，以和糴使韓重華為副。

translations.literal: He was old friends with Wu Yuanheng; when Yuanheng became chief minister, Mengyang was recalled as Vice Minister of Revenue with charge of the revenue bureau, and also made commissioner of the five northern capital farm colonies, with Han Chonghua as deputy grain-purchase commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: An old friend of Wu Yuanheng, he was recalled when Yuanheng became chief minister to serve as vice minister of revenue overseeing the bureau, and as commissioner of the five northern capital farm colonies, with Han Chonghua as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 太府卿王遂與孟陽不協，議以營田非便，持之不下，孟陽忿憾形於言。

translations.literal: Grand Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granary Wang Sui was at odds with Mengyang; he argued that the farm colonies were ill-advised and held up the proposal, and Mengyang's resentment showed plainly in his words.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui, grand minister of the imperial granary, opposed Mengyang and argued that the farm colonies were a bad idea, blocking the plan; Mengyang's resentment showed in his speech.

sentences.zh: 二人俱請對，上怒不許，乃罷孟陽為左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Both men asked for an audience; the emperor was angry and refused, and Mengyang was dismissed to Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Both requested an audience; the emperor refused in anger and demoted Mengyang to left regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 明年，復拜戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: The next year he was again appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was reappointed vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 孟陽氣尚豪俊，不拘小節。

translations.literal: Mengyang's temperament favored bold grandeur and he did not trouble himself over small matters.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyang had a bold, grand manner and scorned petty concerns.

sentences.zh: 居第頗極華峻。

translations.literal: His residence was extremely splendid and lofty.
translations.idiomatic: His mansion was extravagantly grand.

sentences.zh: 憲宗微行至樂遊原，見其宏敞，工猶未已，問之。

translations.literal: Xianzong made an incognito visit to Leyou Plain, saw how vast it was with work still unfinished, and asked about it.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong went incognito to Leyou Plain, saw the vast unfinished mansion, and asked whose it was.

sentences.zh: 左右以孟陽對，孟陽懼而罷工作。

translations.literal: His attendants named Mengyang, and Mengyang, in fear, halted the construction.
translations.idiomatic: Told it was Mengyang's, Mengyang in fear stopped the work.

sentences.zh: 性喜宴，公卿朝士多與之遊，時指怒者不一。

translations.literal: He loved banquets; many ministers and court officials associated with him, and at the time fingers were pointed at him in more ways than one.
translations.idiomatic: He loved feasting, and many officials kept his company; at the time criticism of him was widespread.

sentences.zh: 俄以風緩不能行，改左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon, because wind paralysis left him unable to walk, he was changed to Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon wind paralysis left him unable to walk, and he was reassigned as left regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 元和十年八月卒，贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the tenth year of Yuanhe he died and was posthumously granted Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of Yuanhe 10 and was posthumously made minister of war.

sentences.zh: 憲宗每事求理，常發江淮宣慰使，左司郎中鄭敬奉使。

translations.literal: Whenever Xianzong sought good governance, he would dispatch pacification commissioners to the Jianghuai region; Left Bureau Director Zheng Jing was sent on such a mission.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong often sent Jianghuai pacification commissioners when he sought good governance; Left Bureau Director Zheng Jing received such an appointment.

sentences.zh: 辭，上誡之曰：「朕宮中用度，一匹已上皆有簿籍，唯賑恤貧民，無所計算。

translations.literal: On taking leave, the emperor admonished him: "In my palace household accounts, every single bolt of cloth and more is recorded in the ledgers. Only relief for the poor is given without reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: On his departure the emperor warned him: "In my palace accounts, every bolt of cloth and more is entered in the ledgers. Only aid to the poor is dispensed without calculation.

sentences.zh: 卿經明行修，今登車傳命，宜體吾懷，勿學潘孟陽奉使，所至但務酣飲、遊山寺而已。」

translations.literal: You are learned in the classics and upright in conduct. Now you set out bearing my commission—you should enter into my intent, and do not imitate Pan Mengyang on his mission, who wherever he went did nothing but drink himself drunk and tour mountain temples."
translations.idiomatic: You are learned and upright. Now you go bearing my commission—honor my intent, and do not imitate Pan Mengyang on his mission, who did nothing wherever he went but drink and visit mountain temples."

sentences.zh: 其為人主所薄如此！

translations.literal: Such was the contempt in which the sovereign held him!
translations.idiomatic: So lightly did the emperor regard him!

sentences.zh: 李翛，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Li Xiao—his origins are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiao's origins are unknown.

sentences.zh: 起於寒賤，以莊憲皇后妹婿，元和已來驟階仕進。

translations.literal: Rising from poverty and low status, he became the brother-in-law of Empress Dowager Zhuangxian and from the Yuanhe era onward rose rapidly in office.
translations.idiomatic: Born poor and obscure, he became brother-in-law to Empress Dowager Zhuangxian and from the Yuanhe era rose swiftly in rank.

sentences.zh: 以恩澤至坊州、絳州刺史。

translations.literal: Through imperial favor he reached the governorships of Fang and Jiang Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial favor raised him to govern Fang and Jiang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 無他才，性纖巧承迎。

translations.literal: He had no other talent, but was finely crafty in flattery.
translations.idiomatic: He had no real ability, only a knack for crafty flattery.

sentences.zh: 常飾廚傳以奉往來中使及禁軍中尉賓客，以求善譽。

translations.literal: He often furnished kitchens and relay stations to entertain traveling palace eunuchs and the guests of the commanders of the imperial guard, seeking good repute.
translations.idiomatic: He often lavishly provisioned relay stations to entertain traveling eunuchs and the guests of the imperial guard commanders, seeking praise.

sentences.zh: 治民蒞事，粗有政能。

translations.literal: In governing the people and handling affairs he had a rough competence in administration.
translations.idiomatic: In governing people and handling affairs he showed a rough administrative competence.

sentences.zh: 上以為才，召拜司農卿，遷京兆尹。

translations.literal: The emperor considered him talented and summoned him as Minister of Agriculture, then made him metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought him capable and made him minister of agriculture, then metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 十年，莊憲太后崩，翛為山陵橋道置頓使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when Empress Dowager Zhuangxian died, Xiao was made commissioner for imperial tomb roads and relay stations.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when Empress Dowager Zhuangxian died, Xiao was appointed commissioner for the tomb road and relay stations.

sentences.zh: 恃能惜費，每事減損。

translations.literal: Relying on his ability and stinting on expense, he cut back on everything.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his thrift, he cut costs at every turn.

sentences.zh: 靈駕至灞橋頓，從官多不得食。

translations.literal: When the imperial coffin reached the Bashiqiao relay station, many of the attending officials went without food.
translations.idiomatic: At the Bashiqiao relay station, many attending officials had nothing to eat.

sentences.zh: 及至渭城北門，門壞。

translations.literal: When they reached the north gate of Wei Prefecture, the gate collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: At Wei's north gate, the gate gave way.

sentences.zh: 先是，橋道司請改造渭城北門，計錢三萬。

translations.literal: Earlier the tomb-road office had requested rebuilding Wei's north gate, estimated at thirty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the tomb-road office had asked to rebuild Wei's north gate at a cost of thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 翛以勞費不從，令深鑿軌道以通靈駕。

translations.literal: Xiao, deeming the labor and expense excessive, refused and ordered the track deepened to pass the imperial coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao refused, calling it too costly, and ordered the road cut deeper to pass the coffin through.

sentences.zh: 掘土既深，旁柱皆懸，因而頓壞，所不及邅辌車者數步而已。

translations.literal: Once the earth was dug deep, the side posts hung unsupported, and the gate therefore collapsed; the coffin carriage missed being blocked by only a few paces.
translations.idiomatic: Digging deep left the side posts hanging; the gate collapsed, and the coffin carriage missed being blocked by only a few steps.

sentences.zh: 初欲壞城之東北墉，以出靈駕，中人皆不可，乃停駕，徹去壞門土木而後行。

translations.literal: At first he intended to breach the northeast wall to let the coffin pass, but the eunuchs all objected; they halted the procession, removed the ruined gate's timbers and earth, and then proceeded.
translations.idiomatic: He first planned to break the northeast wall to let the coffin through, but the eunuchs objected; the procession halted while ruined gate timbers and earth were cleared away.

sentences.zh: 翛懼，誣奏邅辌軸折，山陵使李逢吉令御史封其車軸，自陵還，奏請免翛官。

translations.literal: Xiao, in fear, falsely reported that a coffin carriage axle had broken; tomb commissioner Li Fengji ordered the censors to seal the axle, and on returning from the tomb requested that Xiao be dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing blame, Xiao falsely reported a broken coffin axle; tomb commissioner Li Fengji had censors seal the axle and, on return from the tomb, asked that Xiao be removed from office.

sentences.zh: 上以用兵務集財賦，以翛前後進奉，不之責，但罰俸而已。

translations.literal: Because the emperor was waging war and needed to gather revenue, and because Xiao had repeatedly presented tribute, he was not punished but only fined a portion of his salary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, needing revenue for the war and mindful of Xiao's past tribute, did not punish him but only fined his salary.

sentences.zh: 逢吉極言其罪，乃削銀青階。

translations.literal: Fengji pressed his guilt to the limit, and Xiao was stripped of his silver and purple rank.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji pressed the case hard, and Xiao lost his silver-purple rank.

sentences.zh: 翌日，復賜金紫。

translations.literal: The next day he was again granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: The next day gold and purple were restored to him.

sentences.zh: 自此，朝廷端士，多遭譖毀，義士為之側目。

translations.literal: From then on upright men of the court were often slandered, and men of principle looked on with dismay.
translations.idiomatic: After that, upright court officials were often slandered, and men of principle looked on in dismay.

sentences.zh: 時宿師於野，饋運不集。

translations.literal: At the time troops were encamped in the field and supplies failed to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were encamped in the field while supplies failed to reach them.

sentences.zh: 浙西重鎮，號為殷阜，乃以翛為潤州刺史、浙西觀察使，令設法鳩聚財貨。

translations.literal: Zhexi was a major command, known as prosperous and fertile, and Xiao was therefore made governor of Run Prefecture and military commissioner of Zhexi, with orders to devise means to amass wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhexi was a wealthy key command, and Xiao was made governor of Run and commissioner of Zhexi to devise ways to gather wealth.

sentences.zh: 淮西用兵，頗賴其賦。

translations.literal: The campaign against Huaixi relied heavily on his levies.
translations.idiomatic: The Huaixi campaign depended heavily on his taxes.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以病求還京師，未朝謁而卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he asked to return to the capital on account of illness and died before he could attend court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he sought to return to the capital because of illness and died before attending court.

sentences.zh: 王遂，宰相方慶之孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Sui was the grandson of Chief Minister Fangqing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui was the grandson of Chief Minister Fangqing.

sentences.zh: 以吏能聞於時。

translations.literal: He was known in his time for administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 尤長於興利，銳於操下，法頗嚴酷。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled at promoting profit, sharp in controlling subordinates, and his methods were quite harsh.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at revenue, was severe with subordinates, and ruled harshly.

sentences.zh: 累遷至鄧州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to governor of Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to governor of Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以曉達錢穀，入為太府卿。

translations.literal: Because he understood finances, he entered court as Grand Minister of the Imperial Granary.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in finance, he entered court as grand minister of the imperial granary.

sentences.zh: 潘孟陽判度支，與遂私憾，互有爭論。

translations.literal: Pan Mengyang oversaw the revenue bureau and had a private grudge against Sui; they argued with each other.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Mengyang, overseeing the revenue bureau, bore a private grudge against Sui and they quarreled.

sentences.zh: 遂為西北供軍使，言營田非便，與孟陽會議相非，各求請對。

translations.literal: Sui was northwest supply commissioner and argued that the farm colonies were ill-advised; he and Mengyang met in conference and denounced each other, each asking for an audience.
translations.idiomatic: As northwest supply commissioner, Sui opposed the farm colonies; he and Mengyang denounced each other in conference and each sought an audience.

sentences.zh: 上怒，俱不見，出遂為柳州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and received neither; Sui was sent out as governor of Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused both audiences in anger and sent Sui out as governor of Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 遂親吏韋行素、柳季常請課料於兩池務。

translations.literal: Sui's personal clerks Wei Xingsu and Liu Jichang requested operating funds from the two pool offices.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's personal clerks Wei Xingsu and Liu Jichang sought operating funds from the two pool offices.

sentences.zh: 屬遂罷務，季常等為吏所誣，各笞四十。

translations.literal: When Sui left office, Jichang and the others were falsely accused by clerks and each received forty blows of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: After Sui left office, Jichang and the others were framed by clerks and each flogged forty strokes.

sentences.zh: 遂柳州制出，左丞呂元膺執奏曰：「遂以補吏犯贓，法當從坐。

translations.literal: When Sui's Liuzhou appointment was issued, Left Vice Director Lü Yuanying submitted a memorial saying: "Sui appointed a clerk who committed corruption; by law he should be punished as an accomplice.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui's Liuzhou appointment was issued, Left Vice Director Lü Yuanying memorialized: "Sui appointed a corrupt clerk and should be punished as an accomplice by law.

sentences.zh: 其除官制雲『清能業官』，據遂犯狀，不宜有『清』字。

translations.literal: His dismissal edict reads 'upright and capable in office'—given Sui's offenses, the word 'upright' is inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: The edict calls him 'upright and capable in office'—given his offenses, 'upright' is inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 柳州大郡，出守為優。

translations.literal: Liuzhou is a large prefecture; to be sent out as its governor is a favor.
translations.idiomatic: Liuzhou is a major prefecture; sending him there as governor is already a favor.

sentences.zh: 謹封還制書。」

translations.literal: I respectfully return the edict unopened."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully return the edict unopened."

sentences.zh: 上令喻之，方行。

translations.literal: The emperor had him persuaded, and only then did Sui depart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him persuaded, and Sui then departed.

sentences.zh: 數年，用兵淮西。

translations.literal: Several years later troops were deployed against Huaixi.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later the court campaigned against Huaixi.

sentences.zh: 天子藉錢穀吏以集財賦，知遂強幹，乃用為宣州刺史、宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven relied on finance officials to gather revenue; knowing Sui was forceful and capable, he was made governor of Xuan Prefecture and military commissioner of Xuanchen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relied on finance officials to gather revenue; knowing Sui was forceful, he made him governor of Xuan and commissioner of Xuanchen.

sentences.zh: 淮、蔡平，王師東討，召拜光祿卿，充淄青行營諸軍糧料使。

translations.literal: When Huai and Cai were pacified and the imperial army marched east, Sui was summoned as Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and made grain commissioner for the Ziqing campaign army.
translations.idiomatic: After Huai and Cai were pacified and the army marched east, Sui was made minister of imperial sacrifices and grain commissioner for the Ziqing campaign.

sentences.zh: 以光祿職當祠祭，改檢校左散騎常侍、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Because the Minister of Imperial Sacrifices' duties were ritual sacrifice, he was changed to Supervisory Left Regular Attendant and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Because the minister of sacrifices handled ritual offerings, he was reassigned as supervisory left regular attendant and censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 初，師之出也，歲計兵食三百萬石。

translations.literal: When the army first set out, annual grain requirements were estimated at three million piculs.
translations.idiomatic: When the army set out, annual grain needs were estimated at three million piculs.

sentences.zh: 及鄆賊誅，遂進羨余一百萬，上以為能。

translations.literal: When the Yan rebels were executed, Sui presented a surplus of one million piculs, and the emperor considered him capable.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan rebels were killed, Sui reported a surplus of one million piculs, and the emperor praised his ability.

sentences.zh: 時分師道所據十二州為三鎮，乃以遂為沂州刺史、沂兗海等州觀察使。

translations.literal: At the time the twelve prefectures held by Li Shidao were divided into three commands, and Sui was made governor of Yi Prefecture and military commissioner of Yi, Yan, and Hai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao's twelve prefectures were then divided into three commands, and Sui became governor of Yi and commissioner of Yi, Yan, and Hai.

sentences.zh: 遂性狷忿，不存大體。

translations.literal: Sui's nature was narrow and resentful; he did not keep the larger picture in view.
translations.idiomatic: Sui was narrow-minded and resentful and lacked a broad view.

sentences.zh: 而軍州民吏，久染汙俗，率多獷戾，而遂數因公事訾詈將卒曰「反虜」，將卒不勝其忿。

translations.literal: The army, officials, and people of the command had long been steeped in corrupt custom and were mostly fierce and unruly; Sui repeatedly rebuked officers and soldiers in public affairs, calling them "rebel bandits," and the troops could not bear their anger.
translations.idiomatic: The command's soldiers, officials, and people had long been steeped in corruption and were fierce; Sui repeatedly berated officers and soldiers in official business, calling them 'rebel bandits,' and they could not endure it.

sentences.zh: 牙將王弁乘人心怨怒，十四年七月，遂方宴集，弁噪集其徒，害遂於席，判官張實、李甫等同遇害。

translations.literal: Adjutant Wang Bian seized on popular resentment; in the seventh month of the fourteenth year, while Sui was at a banquet, Bian roused his followers and killed Sui at the table; Registrar Zhang Shi, Li Fu, and others were killed with him.
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant Wang Bian seized on popular anger; in the seventh month of the fourteenth year, while Sui was feasting, Bian roused his men and killed Sui at the table; Registrar Zhang Shi, Li Fu, and others died with him.

sentences.zh: 及曹華代遂至鎮，盡擒亂黨王弁等誅之。

translations.literal: When Cao Hua replaced Sui at the command, he captured the rebels Wang Bian and the rest and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Hua replaced Sui, he captured Wang Bian and the other rebels and executed them.

sentences.zh: 遂器用不弘，僻於聚斂，而非兼撫之才。

translations.literal: Sui's capacity was not broad; he was obsessed with gathering wealth and lacked the talent to govern and comfort as well.
translations.idiomatic: Sui lacked breadth of mind, obsessed over revenue, and had no gift for governing and comforting men.

sentences.zh: 但峻威刑，以繩亂俗。

translations.literal: He relied only on harsh punishments to restrain a disorderly people.
translations.idiomatic: He relied only on harsh punishments to restrain a lawless people.

sentences.zh: 其所制笞杖，率逾常制。

translations.literal: The beating staffs he prescribed generally exceeded the usual standard.
translations.idiomatic: The beating staffs he prescribed usually exceeded the normal measure.

sentences.zh: 遂既死，監軍使封其杖進呈。

translations.literal: After Sui died, the army supervisor sealed his staffs and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: After Sui's death, the army supervisor sealed his staffs and presented them to court.

sentences.zh: 上令出示於朝，以誡廉使。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered them displayed at court as a warning to surveillance commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had them displayed at court as a warning to surveillance commissioners.

sentences.zh: 曹華，宋州楚丘人，仕宣武軍為牙校。

translations.literal: Cao Hua, a native of Chuqiu in Song Prefecture, served in the Xuanwu Army as a junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hua of Chuqiu in Song Prefecture served in the Xuanwu Army as a junior officer.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，吳少誠叛，本軍以華驍果有智算，用為襄城戍將。

translations.literal: Late in the Zhenyuan era Wu Shaoqing rebelled; the army, because Hua was brave, resolute, and clever in planning, used him as garrison commander at Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhenyuan, when Wu Shaoqing rebelled, the army made the brave and clever Hua garrison commander at Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 蔡賊攻襄城，華屢敗之，德宗特賜旗甲。

translations.literal: When Cai rebels attacked Xiangcheng, Hua repeatedly defeated them, and Dezong specially granted him banners and armor.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai rebels attacked Xiangcheng, Hua repeatedly defeated them, and Dezong personally granted him banners and armor.

sentences.zh: 元和九年，以功授寧州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanhe he was appointed governor of Ning Prefecture for his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 9 he was made governor of Ning Prefecture for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 未行而吳元濟叛，朝廷命河陽帥烏重胤討賊。

translations.literal: Before he departed Wu Yuanji rebelled, and the court ordered Heyang commander Wu Zhongyin to campaign against the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, Wu Yuanji rebelled, and the court ordered Heyang commander Wu Zhongyin against him.

sentences.zh: 重胤請華為懷汝節度行營副使。

translations.literal: Zhongyin asked that Hua serve as deputy campaign commander of the Hua-Ru command.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyin asked that Hua serve as deputy campaign commander of the Hua-Ru command.

sentences.zh: 前後數十戰，大破賊於青陵城。

translations.literal: After dozens of battles he inflicted a great defeat on the rebels at Qingling City.
translations.idiomatic: After dozens of battles he routed the rebels at Qingling City.

sentences.zh: 賊平，授棣州刺史，封陳留郡王。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified he was appointed governor of Di Prefecture and enfeoffed as Prince of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were pacified he became governor of Di and was enfeoffed Prince of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 棣鄰於鄆，賊屢侵逼，華招募群盜之勁者，補之軍卒，分據要路。

translations.literal: Di bordered Yan; rebels repeatedly raided, and Hua recruited the strongest among bandit gangs and enrolled them as soldiers, stationing them along key routes.
translations.idiomatic: Di bordered Yan; rebels raided repeatedly, and Hua recruited the strongest bandits as soldiers and posted them along key routes.

sentences.zh: 其後，賊至皆擊敗之，鄆人不敢北顧。

translations.literal: Afterward whenever rebels came they were beaten back, and the people of Yan dared not look north.
translations.idiomatic: After that rebels were beaten back whenever they came, and the people of Yan dared not look north.

sentences.zh: 及李師道誅，分所管十二州為三鎮。

translations.literal: When Li Shidao was executed the twelve prefectures under his control were divided into three commands.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shidao was executed, his twelve prefectures were divided into three commands.

sentences.zh: 王遂為沂兗海觀察使，褊刻不能馭眾，為牙將王弁所害，朝廷遂授華左散騎常侍、沂州刺史、沂海兗觀察使。

translations.literal: Wang Sui was military commissioner of Yi, Yan, and Hai; narrow and harsh, he could not control his troops and was killed by adjutant Wang Bian; the court then appointed Hua Supervisory Left Regular Attendant, governor of Yi Prefecture, and military commissioner of Yi, Hai, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui, commissioner of Yi, Yan, and Hai, was narrow and harsh, failed to control his troops, and was killed by adjutant Wang Bian; the court then appointed Hua supervisory left regular attendant, governor of Yi, and commissioner of Yi, Hai, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 華至鎮，視事三日，宴將吏，伏甲士千人於幕下。

translations.literal: When Hua reached the command, on the third day of assuming office he feasted the officers and hid a thousand armored soldiers beneath the tent.
translations.idiomatic: Hua reached the command and on his third day in office feasted the officers with a thousand armored soldiers hidden beneath the tent.

sentences.zh: 群校既集，華喻之曰：「吾受命廉問，奉聖旨，以鄆州將士分割三處，有道途轉徙之勞。

translations.literal: When the officers had assembled, Hua addressed them: "I have received a commission to investigate and report, and by imperial order the Yanzhou troops are to be divided among three posts, with the hardship of travel and relocation.
translations.idiomatic: When the officers had gathered, Hua addressed them: "I am commissioned to investigate, and by imperial order the Yanzhou troops are divided among three posts after the hardship of relocation.

sentences.zh: 今有頒給，北州兵稍厚。

translations.literal: There are distributions today; the northern prefecture soldiers receive somewhat more.
translations.idiomatic: There are distributions today; soldiers of the northern prefectures receive somewhat more.

sentences.zh: 鄆州士卒處右，州兵處左，冀易以區別。」

translations.literal: Yanzhou soldiers stand on the right, prefecture soldiers on the left, so they may be easily distinguished."
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou soldiers stand on the right and prefecture soldiers on the left, so they may be easily distinguished."

sentences.zh: 分定，並令州兵出外。

translations.literal: Once the division was set, he ordered the prefecture soldiers to go outside.
translations.idiomatic: Once the division was set, he ordered the prefecture soldiers outside.

sentences.zh: 既出闔門，乃謂鄆卒曰：「天子深知鄆人之勞，然前害主帥者，不能免罪。」

translations.literal: After they had passed through the gate and it was closed, he said to the Yan soldiers: "The Son of Heaven knows well the labors of the people of Yan; yet those who earlier killed their commander cannot escape punishment."
translations.idiomatic: After they had left and the gate was closed, he told the Yan soldiers: "The Son of Heaven knows the labors of the people of Yan; yet those who killed their commander cannot escape punishment."

sentences.zh: 甲士自幕中出，周環之，凡鄆一千二百人，立斬於庭，血流成渠。

translations.literal: Armored soldiers emerged from beneath the tent and surrounded them; all twelve hundred Yan soldiers were beheaded in the courtyard, and blood formed a channel.
translations.idiomatic: Armored soldiers emerged from beneath the tent and surrounded them; all twelve hundred Yan soldiers were beheaded in the courtyard until blood formed a channel.

sentences.zh: 是日，門屏之間，有赤霧高丈余，久之方散。

translations.literal: That day between gate and screen a red mist rose more than ten feet high and only after a long while dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: That day a red mist more than ten feet high rose between gate and screen and lingered long before dispersing.

sentences.zh: 自是海、沂之人，重足股栗，無敢為盜者。

translations.literal: From then on the people of Hai and Yi walked as if on thin ice, trembling in their legs, and none dared become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the people of Hai and Yi trembled with fear and none dared turn bandit.

sentences.zh: 華惡沂之地褊，請移理於兗，許之。

translations.literal: Hua disliked the narrowness of Yi territory and asked to move his seat of government to Yan; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Hua disliked Yi's cramped territory and asked to move his seat to Yan; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 初，李正己盜有青、鄆十二州，傳襲四世，垂五十年，人俗頑驁，不知禮教。

translations.literal: Earlier Li Zhengji had seized the twelve prefectures of Qing and Yan, passing them down through four generations for nearly fifty years; the people were stubborn and fierce and knew nothing of ritual instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhengji had seized Qing and Yan's twelve prefectures, passing them through four generations for nearly fifty years; the people were stubborn and knew no ritual instruction.

sentences.zh: 華令將吏曰：「鄒、魯儒者之鄉，不宜忘於禮義。」

translations.literal: Hua ordered his officers: "Zou and Lu are the homeland of Confucian scholars; one must not forget ritual and righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Hua told his officers: "Zou and Lu are the homeland of Confucian scholars; ritual and righteousness must not be forgotten."

sentences.zh: 乃躬禮儒士，習俎豆之容，春秋釋奠於孔子廟，立學講經，儒冠四集。

translations.literal: He personally honored Confucian scholars, practiced the rites of vessel and stand, performed spring and autumn sacrifices at Confucius's temple, established schools to lecture on the classics, and scholars gathered from all sides.
translations.idiomatic: He personally honored scholars, practiced ritual forms, performed spring and autumn sacrifices at Confucius's temple, established schools for lecturing on the classics, and scholars gathered from all sides.

sentences.zh: 出家財贍給，俾成名入仕，其往者如歸。

translations.literal: He spent his private wealth to support them, enabling them to win fame and enter office; those who came went as if returning home.
translations.idiomatic: He spent private wealth to support them so they might win fame and enter office; those who came felt as if returning home.

sentences.zh: 及鎮州軍亂，殺田弘正，華表請以本軍進討，就加檢校工部尚書，升兗海為武寧節度，賜之節鉞。

translations.literal: When the Zhenzhou army rebelled and killed Tian Hongzheng, Hua memorialized asking to advance with his own army to suppress them; he was additionally made Supervisory Minister of Works, Yan and Hai were elevated to the Wu-Ning command, and he was granted the command baton.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhenzhou army rebelled and killed Tian Hongzheng, Hua asked to advance with his own troops; he was made supervisory minister of works, Yan and Hai were elevated to the Wu-Ning command, and he received the command baton.

sentences.zh: 李絺叛於大梁，華不俟命赴討。

translations.literal: When Li Xi rebelled at Daliang, Hua did not wait for orders and marched to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xi rebelled at Daliang, Hua marched to suppress him without waiting for orders.

sentences.zh: 絺方遣兵三千人取宋州，華逆擊敗之。

translations.literal: Xi had just sent three thousand men to take Song Prefecture when Hua intercepted and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: As Xi sent three thousand men to take Song Prefecture, Hua intercepted and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 由是，宋、亳不從絺亂。

translations.literal: Because of this Song and Bo did not join Xi's rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this Song and Bo did not join Xi's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 絺平，以功加檢校尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: When Xi was pacified, Hua was additionally made Supervisory Right Vice Director for his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi was pacified, Hua was additionally made supervisory right vice director for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 以河朔拒命，移華為滑州刺史、義成軍節度使。

translations.literal: Because the Hebei region defied orders, Hua was transferred to governor of Hua Prefecture and military governor of the Yicheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: Because Hebei defied orders, Hua was transferred to governor of Hua and military governor of the Yicheng Army.

sentences.zh: 長慶三年七月，卒於鎮，時年六十九。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year of Changqing he died in command at the age of sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in command in the seventh month of Changqing 3, aged sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 華雖出自戎行，而動必由禮。

translations.literal: Although Hua came from the military profession, his actions always followed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Though Hua came from the ranks, his conduct always followed ritual.

sentences.zh: 尤重士大夫，未嘗以富貴驕人；

translations.literal: He especially valued scholar-officials and never showed arrogance because of wealth and rank;
translations.idiomatic: He especially valued scholar-officials and never flaunted wealth or rank;

sentences.zh: 下迨仆隸走使之徒，必待之以誠信，人以為難。

translations.literal: even down to servants and runners he always treated them with sincerity and trust, which people found difficult.
translations.idiomatic: even servants and runners he treated with sincerity and trust, which people found remarkable.

sentences.zh: 贈司空。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 韋綬，字子章，京兆人。

translations.literal: Wei Shou, styled Zizhang, was a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou, styled Zizhang, was from Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 少有至性，喪父，刺血寫佛經。

translations.literal: From youth he had utmost filial nature; when his father died he pricked his finger and wrote out a Buddhist sutra in blood.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was deeply filial; when his father died he pricked his finger and copied a Buddhist sutra in blood.

sentences.zh: 初為長安縣尉，遭硃泚之亂，變服乘驢赴奉天。

translations.literal: He first served as magistrate of Chang'an County; during Zhu Ci's rebellion he changed clothes and rode a donkey to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as magistrate of Chang'an; during Zhu Ci's rebellion he changed clothes and rode a donkey to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 於頔鎮襄陽，辟為賓佐。

translations.literal: When Yu Di governed Xiangyang he recruited him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Di governed Xiangyang, he recruited Shou as an aide.

sentences.zh: 嘗因言政，面刺頔之縱恣。

translations.literal: Once, while discussing government, he openly reproached Di's indulgence and license.
translations.idiomatic: Once, discussing government, he openly reproached Di's indulgence.

sentences.zh: 入朝為工部員外，轉屯田郎中。

translations.literal: He entered court as Assistant in the Ministry of Works and was transferred to Bureau Director of the Directorate of Imperial Parks.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as assistant in the Ministry of Works and became bureau director of imperial parks.

sentences.zh: 元和十年，改職方郎中，充太子諸王侍讀，再遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yuanhe he was changed to Bureau Director of the Bureau of Appointments, served as lecturer to the crown prince and imperial princes, and was twice promoted to Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 10 he became bureau director of appointments, lectured to the crown prince and imperial princes, and was twice promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 時穆宗在東宮，方幼好戲。

translations.literal: At the time Muzong was in the Eastern Palace and, still young, loved play.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Muzong was in the Eastern Palace and, still young, loved games.

sentences.zh: 綬講書之隙，頗以嘲誚悅之。

translations.literal: In the intervals of Shou's lectures he often amused him with mockery and jest.
translations.idiomatic: Between lectures Shou often amused him with mockery and jest.

sentences.zh: 嘗密賫家所造食，入宮餉太子。

translations.literal: Once he secretly brought food made at home into the palace to present to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Once he secretly brought homemade food into the palace for the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 憲宗嘗召對，綬奏曰：「太子學書，至『依』字，輒去旁『人』。

translations.literal: Xianzong once summoned him for audience, and Shou reported: "When the crown prince studies writing, whenever he reaches the character 'yi' he removes the side element 'ren'.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong once summoned him, and Shou reported: "When the crown prince studies writing, whenever he reaches the character yi he removes the side element ren.

sentences.zh: 臣問之，太子云：『君父以此字可天下奏事，臣子不合全書。』」

translations.literal: I asked him why, and the crown prince said: 'Sovereign and father may use this character in memorials to the throne throughout the realm; a subject should not write it whole.'"
translations.idiomatic: I asked why, and the crown prince said: 'Sovereign and father may use this character in memorials throughout the realm; a subject should not write it whole.'"

sentences.zh: 上益嘉太子之賢，賜綬錦彩。

translations.literal: The emperor was all the more pleased with the crown prince's virtue and granted Shou brocade and silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was all the more pleased with the crown prince's virtue and rewarded Shou with brocade and silk.

sentences.zh: 綬無威儀，時以人間鄙說戲言以取悅太子。

translations.literal: Shou had no dignity of bearing; at the time he used vulgar street tales and jesting words to please the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Shou lacked dignified bearing and used vulgar street tales and jests to please the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子因入侍，道綬語。

translations.literal: The crown prince, while attending the emperor, repeated Shou's words.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince repeated Shou's words while attending the emperor.

sentences.zh: 憲宗不悅，謂侍臣曰：「凡侍讀者，當以經義輔導太子，納之輒物，而綬語及此，予何望耶？」

translations.literal: Xianzong was displeased and told his attendants: "Any lecturer should use classical meaning to guide the crown prince. He brings trinkets as gifts, yet Shou's words reach even this—what hope can I have?"
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong was displeased and told his attendants: "Lecturers should guide the crown prince with classical meaning. He brings trinkets as gifts, yet Shou's words reach even this—what hope can I have?"

sentences.zh: 乃罷侍讀，出為虔州刺史。

translations.literal: Shou was then dismissed from lecturing and sent out as governor of Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was dismissed from lecturing and sent out as governor of Qian.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，以師友之恩，召為尚書右丞，兼集賢院學士，甚承恩顧，出入禁中。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, because of their bond as teacher and friend he was summoned as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and received great favor, entering and leaving the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the throne, Shou was summoned as right vice director and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies for their teacher-friend bond, and enjoyed great favor within the palace.

sentences.zh: 綬以七月六日是穆宗載誕節，請以是日百官詣光順門賀太后，然後上皇帝壽。

translations.literal: Shou, because the sixth day of the seventh month was Muzong's birthday, asked that on that day all officials first go to Guangshun Gate to congratulate the empress dowager and then wish the emperor long life.
translations.idiomatic: Because the sixth day of the seventh month was Muzong's birthday, Shou asked that officials first congratulate the empress dowager at Guangshun Gate and then wish the emperor long life.

sentences.zh: 時政道頗僻，敕出，人不敢議。

translations.literal: Government was then quite perverse, and when the edict issued no one dared object.
translations.idiomatic: Government was then quite perverse, and when the edict issued no one dared object.

sentences.zh: 久之，宰臣奏古無生日稱賀之儀，其事終寢。

translations.literal: After a long while the chief ministers reported that antiquity had no ritual of congratulating someone on a birthday, and the matter was finally dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually the chief ministers reported that antiquity had no birthday congratulation ritual, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 綬在集賢，遇重陽，賜宰臣百官曲江宴；

translations.literal: While Shou was at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, on Double Ninth the emperor granted a Qujiang banquet to chief ministers and all officials;
translations.idiomatic: While Shou was at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, on Double Ninth the emperor granted a Qujiang banquet to chief ministers and officials;

sentences.zh: 綬請與集賢學士別為一會，從之。

translations.literal: Shou asked that the assembled-worthies academicians hold a separate gathering, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Shou asked that assembled-worthies academicians hold a separate gathering, and this was granted.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年三月，轉禮部尚書，判集賢院事。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Changqing he was transferred to Minister of Rites with charge of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Changqing 1 he became minister of rites with charge of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問：「禳災祈福，其可必乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor once asked: "Can disaster-averting prayer and blessing-seeking be made certain?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked: "Can prayer to avert disaster and seek blessing be made certain?"

sentences.zh: 綬對曰：「昔宋景公以一善言而法星退之三舍，此禳災以德也。

translations.literal: Shou replied: "In antiquity Duke Jing of Song, with one good word, made the baleful star retreat three lodges—this was averting disaster through virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Shou replied: "In antiquity Duke Jing of Song, with one good word, made the baleful star retreat three lodges—disaster averted through virtue.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝除秘祝，每於祠祭，盡敬而已，言無所祈，以明福不可以求致也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han abolished secret prayers; at every sacrifice he was fully reverent and spoke no prayers, showing that fortune cannot be sought and obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han abolished secret prayers; at every sacrifice he was fully reverent and prayed for nothing, showing fortune cannot be sought.

sentences.zh: 而二君卒能變已變之災，享自致之福，著於史傳，其理甚明。

translations.literal: Yet both rulers finally transformed disasters already changed and enjoyed fortune they had brought upon themselves, as recorded in history—the principle is very clear.
translations.idiomatic: Yet both finally transformed disasters and enjoyed self-won fortune, as history records—the principle is clear.

sentences.zh: 如失德以祈災消，媚神以祈福至，神茍有知，當因以致譴，非祈禳之道也。」

translations.literal: If one loses virtue yet prays for disaster to vanish, or flatters the spirits to seek blessing, and the spirits have knowledge, they will bring reproof because of it—this is not the way of prayer and ritual."
translations.idiomatic: If one loses virtue yet prays for disaster to vanish, or flatters spirits to seek blessing, and spirits have knowledge, they will bring reproof—this is not the way of prayer and ritual."

sentences.zh: 時人主失德，綬因以諷之。

translations.literal: The ruler then lacked virtue, and Shou thereby offered indirect reproof.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler then lacked virtue, and Shou offered indirect reproof.

sentences.zh: 二年十月，檢校戶部尚書、興元尹、山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year he was made Supervisory Minister of Revenue, governor of Xingyuan, and military governor of the Western Mountain South circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year he was made supervisory minister of revenue, governor of Xingyuan, and military governor of the Western Mountain South circuit.

sentences.zh: 辭日，請門戟十二，自將赴鎮。

translations.literal: On the day of his farewell audience he requested twelve gate halberds and set out for his command at the head of his own troops.
translations.idiomatic: On his farewell audience he requested twelve gate halberds and set out for his command leading his own troops.

sentences.zh: 又訴家貧，請賜錢二百萬。

translations.literal: He also complained of family poverty and asked for a grant of two million cash.
translations.idiomatic: He also pleaded family poverty and asked for two million cash.

sentences.zh: 又面乞授子元弼官。

translations.literal: He also asked in person that his son Yuanbi be granted office.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked in person that his son Yuanbi receive office.

sentences.zh: 上皆可之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all of these.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of these.

sentences.zh: 綬禦事無術，洎臨戎鎮，庶政隳紊。

translations.literal: Shou had no method in governing affairs; once he took command in the field, civil administration fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Shou had no gift for governing; once he took field command, civil administration fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 二年八月卒，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year he died and was posthumously granted Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of the second year and was posthumously made right vice director.

sentences.zh: 博士劉端夫請謚為「通」，殿中侍御史孟琯上言以為非當。

translations.literal: Erudite Liu Duanfu requested the posthumous title "Tong"; Palace Censor Meng Guan submitted a memorial arguing this was inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Liu Duanfu proposed the posthumous title "Tong"; palace censor Meng Guan argued this was inappropriate.

sentences.zh: 博士權安請謚為「繆」，竟不施行。

translations.literal: Erudite Quan An requested the posthumous title "Miu," but in the end it was not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Quan An proposed the title "Miu," but in the end it was not granted.

sentences.zh: 鄭權，滎陽開封人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Quan was a native of Kaifeng in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Quan was from Kaifeng in Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，釋褐涇原從事。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and on leaving office served as an aide in Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and first served as an aide in Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 節度使劉昌符病亟，請入覲，度軍情必變，以權寬厚容眾，俾主留務。

translations.literal: When Military Governor Liu Changfu was gravely ill he asked to enter court for audience; judging that army sentiment would surely change, he made Quan, broad and tolerant in winning men, oversee remaining affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Military Governor Liu Changfu fell gravely ill and asked to attend court, judging that army sentiment would change, he put the broad and tolerant Quan in charge of remaining affairs.

sentences.zh: 及昌符上路，兵果亂。

translations.literal: Once Changfu was on the road, the soldiers indeed mutinied.
translations.idiomatic: Once Changfu was on the road, the soldiers mutinied.

sentences.zh: 權挺身入白刃中，抗辭喻以逆順。

translations.literal: Quan threw himself into the midst of naked blades and with stern words explained loyalty and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Quan threw himself into naked blades and with stern words explained loyalty and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 因殺其首亂者數人，三軍畏伏。

translations.literal: He then killed several of the chief mutineers, and the three armies submitted in fear.
translations.idiomatic: He then killed several chief mutineers, and the three armies submitted in fear.

sentences.zh: 德宗聞而嘉之。

translations.literal: Dezong heard of it and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong heard of it and praised him.

sentences.zh: 時天子厭兵，籓鎮將吏得軍情者，多超授官爵。

translations.literal: At the time the Son of Heaven was weary of war; command officers and officials who won army sentiment were often promoted far beyond normal rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was weary of war; officers who won army sentiment were often promoted far beyond normal rank.

sentences.zh: 自試衛佐擢授行軍司馬、御史中丞。

translations.literal: From trial guard aide he was promoted to campaign deputy and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: From trial guard aide he was promoted to campaign deputy and censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 入朝為倉部郎中，累遷至河南尹。

translations.literal: He entered court as Bureau Director of the Granary Bureau and was repeatedly promoted to metropolitan governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as granary bureau director and rose to metropolitan governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 十一年，代李遜為襄州刺史、山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he replaced Li Xun as governor of Xiang Prefecture and military governor of the Eastern Mountain South circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he replaced Li Xun as governor of Xiang and military governor of the Eastern Mountain South circuit.

sentences.zh: 十二年，轉華州刺史、潼關防禦、鎮國軍使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to governor of Hua Prefecture, Tong Pass defense commissioner, and Zhenguo Army commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he became governor of Hua, Tong Pass defense commissioner, and Zhenguo Army commander.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遷德州刺史、德棣滄景節度使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to governor of De Prefecture and military governor of De, Di, Cang, and Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he became governor of De and military governor of De, Di, Cang, and Jing.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷用兵討李師道，權以德、棣之兵臨境。

translations.literal: At the time the court was campaigning against Li Shidao, and Quan pressed the armies of De and Di against the border.
translations.idiomatic: While the court campaigned against Li Shidao, Quan pressed the armies of De and Di against the border.

sentences.zh: 奏於平原、安德二縣之間置歸化縣，以集降民。

translations.literal: He memorialized that between Pingyuan and Ande counties a Guihua County be established to gather surrendered people.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that Guihua County be established between Pingyuan and Ande to gather surrendered people.

sentences.zh: 滄州刺史李宗奭與權不協，每事多違，不稟節制。

translations.literal: Cang Prefecture Governor Li Zong'ao was at odds with Quan; on every matter he opposed him and did not follow command.
translations.idiomatic: Cang Prefecture Governor Li Zong'ao opposed Quan on every matter and did not follow command.

sentences.zh: 權奏之，上令中使追之。

translations.literal: Quan reported this, and the emperor ordered a palace eunuch to recall him.
translations.idiomatic: Quan reported this, and the emperor ordered a palace eunuch to recall Zong'ao.

sentences.zh: 宗奭諷州兵留己，上言懼亂，未敢離郡，乃以烏重胤鎮橫海，代權歸朝。

translations.literal: Zong'ao incited the prefectural soldiers to detain him; he reported in fear of disorder and dared not leave the prefecture, and Quan was therefore replaced by Wu Zhongyin governing Heng-Hai and returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: Zong'ao incited prefectural soldiers to detain him; he reported fear of disorder and dared not leave, and Quan was replaced by Wu Zhongyin at Heng-Hai and returned to court.

sentences.zh: 滄州將吏懼，共逐宗奭。

translations.literal: The officers and officials of Cang Prefecture were afraid and together drove out Zong'ao.
translations.idiomatic: Cang's officers and officials, afraid, together drove out Zong'ao.

sentences.zh: 宗奭方奔歸京師。

translations.literal: Zong'ao was just then fleeing back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zong'ao was then fleeing back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔以悖慢之罪，斬於獨柳之下。

translations.literal: An edict condemned him for insolence and disrespect and beheaded him beneath the Lone Willow.
translations.idiomatic: An edict condemned him for insolence and beheaded him beneath the Lone Willow.

sentences.zh: 其弟宗爽，長流汀州。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zongshuang was exiled far to Ting Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zongshuang was exiled to Ting Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 授權邠寧節度。

translations.literal: Quan was appointed military governor of Bin-Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was appointed military governor of Bin-Ning.

sentences.zh: 會天德軍使上章論宗奭之冤，為權誣奏，權降授原王傅。

translations.literal: When the Tiande Army commander memorialized that Zong'ao had been wronged and had been falsely reported by Quan, Quan was demoted to tutor of the Prince of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tiande Army commander memorialized that Zong'ao had been wronged and falsely reported by Quan, Quan was demoted to tutor of the Prince of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 尋遷右金吾衛大將軍，充左街使。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Grand General of the Right Gold Crow Guard and made commander of the Left Street.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became grand general of the Right Gold Crow Guard and commander of the Left Street.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，改左散騎常侍，充入回鶻告哀使。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne he was changed to Left Regular Attendant and made envoy to announce mourning to the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the throne he became left regular attendant and envoy to announce mourning to the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 憚其遠役，辭以足疾，不獲免，肩輿而行。

translations.literal: Fearing the distant mission, he pleaded foot ailment but could not be excused and was carried in a litter.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the distant mission, he pleaded foot ailment but could not be excused and traveled in a litter.

sentences.zh: 權器度魁偉，有辭辯。

translations.literal: Quan was imposing in bearing and had eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was imposing in bearing and eloquent.

sentences.zh: 既至虜廷，與虜主爭論曲直，言辭激壯，可汗深敬異之。

translations.literal: Once he reached the barbarian court he argued right and wrong with the khan; his words were fierce and strong, and the khan deeply respected and marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: At the barbarian court he argued right and wrong with the khan; his words were fierce and strong, and the khan deeply respected him.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年使還。

translations.literal: He returned from his mission in the first year of Changqing.
translations.idiomatic: He returned from his mission in Changqing 1.

sentences.zh: 出為河南尹，入拜工部侍郎，遷本曹尚書。

translations.literal: He was sent out as metropolitan governor of Henan, entered court as Vice Minister of Works, and was promoted to Minister of that bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He served as metropolitan governor of Henan, entered court as vice minister of works, and rose to minister of that bureau.

sentences.zh: 以家人數多，俸入不足，求為鎮守。

translations.literal: Because his household was large and his salary insufficient, he asked for a frontier command.
translations.idiomatic: Because his household was large and his salary insufficient, he asked for a frontier command.

sentences.zh: 旬月，檢校右僕射、廣州刺史、嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: Within ten days he was made Supervisory Right Vice Director, governor of Guang Prefecture, and military governor of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he was made supervisory right vice director, governor of Guang, and military governor of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 初，權出鎮，有中人之助。

translations.literal: At first when Quan went out to command he had the help of eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: When Quan first went out to command he had eunuch backing.

sentences.zh: 南海多珍貨，權頗積聚以遺之，大為朝士所嗤。

translations.literal: The South Sea had many precious goods; Quan amassed them considerably to present to the eunuchs and was greatly ridiculed by court officials.
translations.idiomatic: The South Sea held many precious goods; Quan amassed them to present to eunuchs and was greatly ridiculed by court officials.

sentences.zh: 四年十月卒。

translations.literal: He died in the tenth month of the fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth month of the fourth year.

sentences.zh: 盧士玫，山東右族，以文儒進。

translations.literal: Lu Shimei was of a distinguished Shandong clan and advanced through literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shimei came from a distinguished Shandong clan and advanced through literary learning.

sentences.zh: 性端厚，與物無競，雅有令聞。

translations.literal: His nature was upright and generous; he did not contend with others and had an excellent reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and generous, did not contend with others, and enjoyed an excellent reputation.

sentences.zh: 始為吏部員外郎，稱職，轉郎中、京兆少尹。

translations.literal: He first served as Assistant in the Ministry of Personnel, performed his duties well, was transferred to Bureau Director, and became Junior Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as assistant in the Ministry of Personnel, performed well, became bureau director, and junior metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 奉憲宗園寢，刑簡事集，時論推其有才，權知京兆尹事。

translations.literal: He attended to Xianzong's imperial park tomb; punishments were simple and affairs were gathered, and public opinion praised his talent, so he was given acting charge of the metropolitan governorship.
translations.idiomatic: He attended Xianzong's imperial park tomb with simple punishments and efficient affairs; opinion praised his talent, and he was given acting charge of the metropolitan governorship.

sentences.zh: 會幽州劉總願釋兵柄入朝，請用張弘靖代己。

translations.literal: When Youzhou's Liu Zong wished to relinquish military power and enter court, he asked that Zhang Hongjing replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zong of Youzhou wished to relinquish military power and enter court, he asked that Zhang Hongjing replace him.

sentences.zh: 復請析瀛、漠兩州，用士玫為帥，朝廷一皆從之。

translations.literal: He also asked that Ying and Mo prefectures be separated out and Shimei made their commander; the court approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that Ying and Mo be separated out with Shimei as commander; the court approved all of this.

sentences.zh: 士玫遂授檢校右常侍，充瀛、漠兩州都防禦觀察使。

translations.literal: Shimei was therefore appointed Supervisory Right Regular Attendant and overall defense and surveillance commissioner of Ying and Mo prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei was appointed supervisory right regular attendant and overall defense and surveillance commissioner of Ying and Mo.

sentences.zh: 無何，幽州亂，害賓佐，縶弘靖，取裨將硃克融領軍務，遣兵襲瀛、漠。

translations.literal: Before long Youzhou fell into disorder; aides were killed and Hongjing was seized; the deputy commander Zhu Kerong took military affairs, and troops were sent to attack Ying and Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Youzhou fell into disorder; aides were killed, Hongjing was seized, deputy Zhu Kerong took military affairs, and troops attacked Ying and Mo.

sentences.zh: 朝廷慮防禦之名不足抗兇逆，即日除士玫檢校工部尚書，充瀛漠節度使。

translations.literal: The court feared the title of defense commissioner was insufficient to resist the rebels and that same day made Shimei Supervisory Minister of Works and military governor of Ying and Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the defense title was insufficient against the rebels, the court that same day made Shimei supervisory minister of works and military governor of Ying and Mo.

sentences.zh: 士玫亦罄家財助軍用，堅拒叛徒者累月。

translations.literal: Shimei also exhausted his family wealth to aid military supplies and firmly resisted the rebels for months.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei also exhausted family wealth for military supplies and firmly resisted the rebels for months.

sentences.zh: 竟以官軍救之不至，又瀛漠之卒親愛多在幽州，遂為其下陰導克融之兵以潰。

translations.literal: In the end because imperial relief did not arrive, and because many soldiers of Ying and Mo had kin in Youzhou, his subordinates secretly guided Kerong's troops and the defense collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the end imperial relief did not arrive, and because many Ying and Mo soldiers had kin in Youzhou, his subordinates secretly guided Kerong's troops and the defense collapsed.

sentences.zh: 士玫及從事皆被拘執，送幽州，囚於賓館。

translations.literal: Shimei and his staff were all seized and sent to Youzhou, where they were imprisoned in the guest house.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei and his staff were seized, sent to Youzhou, and imprisoned in the guest house.

sentences.zh: 及朝廷宥克融之罪，士玫方得歸東洛。

translations.literal: When the court pardoned Kerong's crimes, Shimei was finally able to return to eastern Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the court pardoned Kerong's crimes, Shimei was finally able to return to eastern Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 尋拜太子賓客，留司洛中，旋除虢州刺史，復為賓客。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Crown Prince's Mentor, remaining at his post in Luoyang; he was then made governor of Guo Prefecture and again made mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became crown prince's mentor, remaining in Luoyang; he was then made governor of Guo and again mentor.

sentences.zh: 寶歷元年七月卒，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh month of the first year of Baoli and was posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month of Baoli 1 and was posthumously made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 韓全義，出自行間，少從禁軍，事竇文場。

translations.literal: Han Quanyi came from the ranks; in youth he served in the imperial guard under Dou Wenchang.
translations.idiomatic: Han Quanyi came from the ranks; in youth he served in the imperial guard under Dou Wenchang.

sentences.zh: 及文場為中尉，用全義為帳中偏將，典禁兵在長武城。

translations.literal: When Wenchang became army supervisor he used Quanyi as a partial general in his headquarters, commanding imperial guard troops at Changwu Fort.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenchang became army supervisor he made Quanyi a partial general in his headquarters commanding imperial guard troops at Changwu Fort.

sentences.zh: 貞元十三年，為神策行營節度、長武城使，代韓潭為夏綏銀宥節度，詔以長武兵赴鎮。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhenyuan he was made campaign commander of the Divine Strategy Army and commander of Changwu Fort, replacing Han Tan as military governor of Xia, Sui, Yin, and You; an edict ordered the Changwu troops to proceed to command.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 13 he became campaign commander of the Divine Strategy Army and commander of Changwu Fort, replacing Han Tan as military governor of Xia, Sui, Yin, and You; an edict ordered the Changwu troops to proceed to command.

sentences.zh: 全義貪而無勇，短於撫禦。

translations.literal: Quanyi was greedy and lacked courage, and was poor at governing and comforting troops.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi was greedy, lacked courage, and was poor at governing troops.

sentences.zh: 制未下，軍中知之，相與謀曰：「夏州沙磧之地，無耕蠶生業。

translations.literal: Before the edict was issued the army learned of it and together plotted, saying: "Xia Prefecture is sandy desert land; there is no farming or silkworm industry.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict issued the army learned of it and plotted together: "Xia Prefecture is sandy desert; there is no farming or silkworm industry.

sentences.zh: 盛夏移徙，吾所不能。」

translations.literal: To move in the height of summer—we cannot do it."
translations.idiomatic: To move in the height of summer—we cannot do it."

sentences.zh: 是夜，戍卒鼓噪為亂，全義逾城而免，殺其親將王棲巖、趙虔曜等。

translations.literal: That night the garrison soldiers beat drums and clamored in mutiny; Quanyi climbed over the wall and escaped, and his close officers Wang Qiyan and Zhao Qianyao were killed.
translations.idiomatic: That night garrison soldiers mutinied; Quanyi climbed over the wall and escaped, and his close officers Wang Qiyan and Zhao Qianyao were killed.

sentences.zh: 賴都虞候高崇文誅其亂首而止之，全義方獲赴鎮。

translations.literal: Only because Chief Commandant Gao Chongwen executed the ringleaders was the mutiny stopped, and Quanyi was finally able to proceed to command.
translations.idiomatic: Only because Chief Commandant Gao Chongwen executed the ringleaders was the mutiny stopped, and Quanyi finally reached his command.

sentences.zh: 明年，吳少誠拒命，詔征十七鎮之師討之。

translations.literal: The next year Wu Shaoqing defied orders; an edict mobilized the armies of seventeen commands to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Wu Shaoqing defied orders; an edict mobilized armies of seventeen commands against him.

sentences.zh: 時軍無統帥，兵無多少，皆以內官監之，師之進退不由主將。

translations.literal: At the time the army had no supreme commander; regardless of how many troops each had, all were supervised by inner officials, and the army's advance and retreat did not depend on the chief commander.
translations.idiomatic: The army had no supreme commander; regardless of troop numbers, all were supervised by inner officials, and advance and retreat did not depend on the chief commander.

sentences.zh: 十五年冬，王師為賊所敗於小溵河。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifteenth year the imperial army was defeated by the rebels at the Xiao Yin River.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifteenth year the imperial army was defeated by rebels at the Xiao Yin River.

sentences.zh: 德宗以文場素待全義，乃用為蔡州四面行營招討使，仍以陳許節度使上官涚副之。

translations.literal: Dezong, because Wenchang had long favored Quanyi, used him as campaign commander on all sides of Cai Prefecture and made Chenxu Military Governor Shangguan Shui his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wenchang had long favored Quanyi, Dezong made him campaign commander on all sides of Cai and Chenxu Military Governor Shangguan Shui his deputy.

sentences.zh: 諸鎮之師，皆取全義節度。

translations.literal: The armies of all commands took orders from Quanyi.
translations.idiomatic: Armies of all commands took orders from Quanyi.

sentences.zh: 全義將略非所長，能以巧佞財賄結中貴人，以被薦用。

translations.literal: Quanyi was not skilled in strategy but could use crafty flattery and bribes to win inner favorites and thereby win recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi was not skilled in strategy but used crafty flattery and bribes to win inner favorites and recommendation.

sentences.zh: 及師臨賊境，又制在監軍，每議兵出，一帳之中，中人十數，紛然爭論莫決。

translations.literal: Once the army reached rebel territory, control again lay with the army supervisors; whenever they discussed marching out, within one tent a dozen eunuchs argued noisily and no decision could be reached.
translations.idiomatic: Once the army reached rebel territory, army supervisors again held control; whenever they discussed marching out, a dozen eunuchs argued noisily in one tent and no decision could be reached.

sentences.zh: 蔡賊聞之，屢求決戰。

translations.literal: The Cai rebels heard of this and repeatedly sought decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Cai rebels heard of this and repeatedly sought decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 十六年五月，遇賊於溵水南廣利城。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixteenth year they encountered the rebels at Guangli City south of the Yin River.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the sixteenth year they encountered rebels at Guangli City south of the Yin River.

sentences.zh: 旗鼓未交，諸軍大潰，為賊所乘。

translations.literal: Before banners and drums had met, the armies collapsed in great disorder and were pursued by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Before banners and drums met, the armies collapsed in great disorder and were pursued by rebels.

sentences.zh: 全義退保五樓，賊對壘相望。

translations.literal: Quanyi retreated to defend Wulou; the rebels faced his camp across the field.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi retreated to defend Wulou; rebels faced his camp across the field.

sentences.zh: 潰兵未集，乃與監軍賈英秀、賈國良等保溵水縣。

translations.literal: The routed troops had not yet been gathered, and he therefore joined the army supervisors Jia Yingxiu and Jia Guoliang in defending Yinshui County.
translations.idiomatic: Routed troops had not yet been gathered, and he joined army supervisors Jia Yingxiu and Jia Guoliang in defending Yinshui County.

sentences.zh: 賊距溵水五六里而軍，全義懼其淩突，退保陳州。

translations.literal: The rebels encamped five or six li from the Yin River; Quanyi feared their assault and retreated to defend Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels encamped five or six li from the Yin River; Quanyi feared assault and retreated to defend Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其汴宋、河北之軍，皆亡歸本鎮，唯陳許將孟元陽、神策將蘇光榮等數千人守溵水。

translations.literal: The armies of Bian-Song and Hebei all fled back to their own commands; only Chenxu commander Meng Yuanyang, Divine Strategy commander Su Guangrong, and several thousand others held Yinshui.
translations.idiomatic: Bian-Song and Hebei armies fled back to their commands; only Chenxu commander Meng Yuanyang, Divine Strategy commander Su Guangrong, and several thousand others held Yinshui.

sentences.zh: 全義誘潞州大將夏侯仲宣、滑將時昂、河陽將權文度、河中將郭湘等誅之。

translations.literal: Quanyi induced Lu commander Xia Houzhongxuan, Hua commander Shi Ang, Heyang commander Quan Wendu, and Hezhong commander Guo Xiang to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi induced Lu commander Xia Houzhongxuan, Hua commander Shi Ang, Heyang commander Quan Wendu, and Hezhong commander Guo Xiang to execute them.

sentences.zh: 由是軍情稍固。

translations.literal: Because of this army morale gradually stabilized.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this army morale gradually stabilized.

sentences.zh: 少誠知王師無能為，致書幣以告監軍，願求昭洗。

translations.literal: Shaoqing, knowing the imperial army could do nothing, sent letters and gifts to tell the army supervisors he wished to seek rehabilitation.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoqing, knowing the imperial army could do nothing, sent letters and gifts to army supervisors seeking rehabilitation.

sentences.zh: 德宗召大臣議，宰相賈耽曰：「昨全義五樓退軍，賊不追擊者，應望國家恩貸。

translations.literal: Dezong summoned the chief ministers to discuss; Chief Minister Jia Dan said: "Yesterday when Quanyi retreated from Wulou the rebels did not pursue—this should mean they hope for imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong summoned chief ministers to discuss; Chief Minister Jia Dan said: "When Quanyi retreated from Wulou the rebels did not pursue—they likely hope for imperial grace.

sentences.zh: 臣伏恐須開生路。」

translations.literal: I fear we must open a path to life."
translations.idiomatic: I fear we must open a path to life."

sentences.zh: 上然之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 又得監軍等奏，即下制洗滌，加其爵秩。

translations.literal: He also received memorials from the army supervisors and immediately issued an edict of rehabilitation and added to Shaoqing's rank.
translations.idiomatic: He also received memorials from army supervisors and immediately issued rehabilitation and added to Shaoqing's rank.

sentences.zh: 十七年，全義自陳州班師，而中人掩其敗跡，上待之如初。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Quanyi withdrew his army from Chen Prefecture, while the eunuchs concealed his defeat and the emperor treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Quanyi withdrew from Chen Prefecture while eunuchs concealed his defeat and the emperor treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 全義武臣，不達朝儀，托以足疾，不任謁見。

translations.literal: Quanyi was a military man and did not understand court ritual; he pleaded foot ailment and could not perform audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi was a military man who did not understand court ritual; he pleaded foot ailment and avoided audiences.

sentences.zh: 全義司馬崔放入對，德宗勞問，放引過，言招撫無功。

translations.literal: Quanyi's aide Cui Fang entered for audience; Dezong expressed sympathy and asked after him, and Fang accepted blame, saying pacification had achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi's aide Cui Fang entered for audience; Dezong expressed sympathy, and Fang accepted blame, saying pacification had achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 德宗曰：「全義為招討使，招得吳少誠歸國，其功大矣。

translations.literal: Dezong said: "Quanyi as campaign commander pacified Wu Shaoqing's return to the state—his achievement is great.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong said: "Quanyi as campaign commander pacified Wu Shaoqing's return to the state—his achievement is great.

sentences.zh: 何必殺人乃為功耶！」

translations.literal: Why must killing people be counted as achievement?"
translations.idiomatic: Why must killing people count as achievement?"

sentences.zh: 旋命還鎮，令中使就第賜宴，錫賫頗厚。

translations.literal: He was immediately ordered back to command, and a palace eunuch was sent to his residence to grant a banquet with generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately ordered back to command, and a palace eunuch was sent to his residence with a banquet and generous gifts.

sentences.zh: 自還至辭，都不謁見而去。

translations.literal: From his return to his farewell he never performed audience and departed.
translations.idiomatic: From return to farewell he never performed audience and departed.

sentences.zh: 議者以隳敗法制，從古已還，未如貞元之甚。

translations.literal: Critics said the destruction of law had never been so severe since antiquity as in Zhenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said law had never been so thoroughly destroyed since antiquity as in Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 憲宗在籓，常惡其事。

translations.literal: Xianzong, while still a prince, often detested this affair.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong, while still a prince, often detested this affair.

sentences.zh: 及即位，全義懼，求入覲，詔以太子太保致仕。

translations.literal: When he took the throne Quanyi was afraid and asked to enter court; an edict made him Retired Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong took the throne Quanyi was afraid and asked to enter court; an edict made him retired grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 其年七月卒。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh month of that year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month of that year.

sentences.zh: 高霞寓，范陽人。

translations.literal: Gao Xiayi was a native of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xiayi was from Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 祖仙，父棲鶴，皆以孝聞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xian and father Qihe were both famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xian and father Qihe were both famed for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 凡五代同爨。

translations.literal: For five generations they shared one hearth.
translations.idiomatic: For five generations they shared one hearth.

sentences.zh: 德宗朝，采訪使洪經綸奏旌表其門閭，鄉里稱美其事。

translations.literal: In Dezong's reign Investigation Commissioner Hong Jinglun memorialized to honor their gate and lane, and the neighborhood praised the affair.
translations.idiomatic: In Dezong's reign Investigation Commissioner Hong Jinglun memorialized to honor their household, and the neighborhood praised it.

sentences.zh: 霞寓少讀《左氏春秋》及孫、吳《兵法》，好大言，頗以節概自許。

translations.literal: Xiayi in youth read the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals and the military works of Sun and Wu; he loved grand talk and prided himself greatly on integrity and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Xiayi read the Zuo Commentary and the military works of Sun and Wu; he loved grand talk and prided himself on integrity.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，徒步造長武城使高崇文，待以猶子之分，擢授軍職，累奏憲宗，甚見委信。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era he went on foot to visit Changwu Fort commander Gao Chongwen, who treated him like a nephew and promoted him to army office; he repeatedly reported to Xianzong and was greatly trusted.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan he went on foot to Changwu Fort commander Gao Chongwen, who treated him like a nephew, promoted him to army office, and repeatedly reported to Xianzong, winning great trust.

sentences.zh: 元和初，詔授兼御史大夫，從崇文將兵擊劉辟，連戰皆克，下鹿頭城，降李文悅、仇良輔。

translations.literal: Early in Yuanhe an edict appointed him Concurrent Censor-in-Chief; he followed Chongwen in campaigning against Liu Pi, winning successive battles, taking Lutou City, and receiving the surrender of Li Wenye and Qiu Liangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he was made concurrent censor-in-chief; he followed Chongwen against Liu Pi, won successive battles, took Lutou City, and received the surrender of Li Wenye and Qiu Liangfu.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，以功拜彭州刺史，尋繼崇文為長武城使，封感義郡王。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified he was appointed governor of Peng Prefecture for his achievements; he soon succeeded Chongwen as commander of Changwu Fort and was enfeoffed as Prince of Ganyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was pacified he became governor of Peng for his achievements; he soon succeeded Chongwen at Changwu Fort and was enfeoffed Prince of Ganyi.

sentences.zh: 元和五年，以左威衛將軍隨吐突承璀擊王承宗，又加左散騎常侍。
