translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanhe he followed Tuxing Chenghui as Left Weiwu General to attack Wang Chengzong and was additionally made Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 5 he followed Tuxing Chenghui as left Weiwu general against Wang Chengzong and was additionally made left regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 明年，改豐州刺史、三城都團練防禦使。

translations.literal: The next year he was changed to governor of Feng Prefecture and overall training and defense commander of the Three Cities.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became governor of Feng and overall training and defense commander of the Three Cities.

sentences.zh: 六遷至檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted six times to Supervisory Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted six times to supervisory minister of works.

sentences.zh: 元和十年，朝廷討吳元濟，以霞寓宿將，乃析山南東道為兩鎮，以霞寓為唐鄧隋節度使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yuanhe the court campaigned against Wu Yuanji; because Xiayi was a veteran general, the Eastern Mountain South circuit was divided into two commands and Xiayi was made military governor of Tang, Deng, and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 10 the court campaigned against Wu Yuanji; because Xiayi was a veteran general, Eastern Mountain South was divided into two commands and Xiayi became military governor of Tang, Deng, and Sui.

sentences.zh: 霞寓雖稱勇敢，素昧機略；

translations.literal: Although Xiayi was called brave, he had never understood strategy;
translations.idiomatic: Although Xiayi was called brave, he had never understood strategy;

sentences.zh: 至於統制，尤非所長。

translations.literal: as for command and control, he was especially deficient.
translations.idiomatic: in command and control he was especially deficient.

sentences.zh: 及達所部，乃率兵趣蕭陂，與賊決戰。

translations.literal: Once he reached his command he led troops straight to Xiaobo to fight a decisive battle with the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached his command he led troops straight to Xiaobo for a decisive battle with rebels.

sentences.zh: 既小勝，又進至文城柵。

translations.literal: After a small victory he advanced again to Wencheng Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: After a small victory he advanced again to Wencheng Stockade.

sentences.zh: 賊軍偽敗而退，霞寓逐之不已，因為伏兵所掩，王師大衄，霞寓僅以身免。

translations.literal: The rebel army feigned defeat and retreated; Xiayi pursued without cease and was ambushed by hidden troops; the imperial army suffered a great rout and Xiayi barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels feigned defeat and retreated; Xiayi pursued relentlessly, was ambushed, the imperial army suffered a great rout, and Xiayi barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 坐貶歸州刺史。

translations.literal: He was demoted to governor of Gui Prefecture for his offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to governor of Gui for his offense.

sentences.zh: 後以恩例，征為右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Later, by grace precedent, he was summoned as Grand General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Later, by grace precedent, he was summoned as grand general of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 十三年，出為振武節度使，入為左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was sent out as military governor of Zhenwu and entered court as Grand General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was sent out as military governor of Zhenwu and entered court as grand general of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年，授邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing he was appointed military governor of Bin-Ning.
translations.idiomatic: In Changqing 1 he was appointed military governor of Bin-Ning.

sentences.zh: 三年，就加檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: In the third year he was additionally made Supervisory Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was additionally made supervisory right vice director.

sentences.zh: 四年，加檢校司空，又加司徒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was additionally made Supervisory Minister of Works and then Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was additionally made supervisory minister of works and then minister of education.

sentences.zh: 寶歷二年，疽發首，不能理事，求歸闕下。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoli a carbuncle broke out on his head and he could not handle affairs; he asked to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoli 2 a carbuncle broke out on his head and he could not govern; he asked to return to court.

sentences.zh: 其夏，授右金吾衛大將軍、檢校司徒，途次奉天而卒，年五十五，贈太保。

translations.literal: That summer he was appointed Grand General of the Right Gold Crow Guard and Supervisory Minister of Education; he died at Fengtian on the road at the age of fifty-five and was posthumously granted Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he was appointed grand general of the Right Gold Crow Guard and supervisory minister of education; he died on the road at Fengtian, aged fifty-five, and was posthumously made grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 霞寓卒伍常材，始因宦官進用，遂階節將。

translations.literal: Xiayi was common timber from the ranks; he first advanced through eunuch patronage and thus rose to command rank.
translations.idiomatic: Xiayi was common timber from the ranks; he first advanced through eunuch patronage and rose to command rank.

sentences.zh: 位望既高，言多不遜。

translations.literal: Once his position and prospects were high, his words were often disrespectful.
translations.idiomatic: Once his position rose, his words were often disrespectful.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知之，欲議移罷。

translations.literal: The court knew this and intended to discuss transferring and dismissing him.
translations.idiomatic: The court knew this and intended to transfer and dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 霞寓頗懷憂恐，舍私第為佛寺，上言請額為「懷恩」，用資聖福。

translations.literal: Xiayi was quite fearful; he converted his private residence into a Buddhist temple and memorialized asking that it be named "Cherishing Grace" to aid imperial blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiayi grew fearful; he converted his private residence into a Buddhist temple and asked that it be named "Cherishing Grace" to aid imperial blessing.

sentences.zh: 大率奸妄兇狡如此。

translations.literal: In general he was treacherous, false, fierce, and cunning like this.
translations.idiomatic: In general he was treacherous, false, fierce, and cunning.

sentences.zh: 又非斥朝列，侮慢僚屬，鄙辭俚語，日聞於時。

translations.literal: He also did not restrain himself toward court ranks and insulted and slighted colleagues; vulgar and coarse words were heard daily at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He also insulted court ranks and slighted colleagues; vulgar words were heard daily.

sentences.zh: 高瑀，渤海蓚人。

translations.literal: Gao Yu was a native of Su in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yu was from Su in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 少好論兵，釋褐右金吾胄曹，累辟諸府從事，歷陳、蔡二郡刺史，入為太仆卿。

translations.literal: In youth he loved discussing military affairs; on leaving office he served as aide in the Right Gold Crow Guard office and was repeatedly recruited as staff in various offices, serving as governor of Chen and Cai prefectures and entering court as Minister of Imperial Studs.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved military discussion; he first served in the Right Gold Crow Guard office, was recruited to various staffs, governed Chen and Cai, and entered court as minister of imperial studs.

sentences.zh: 太和初，忠武節度使王沛卒，物議以陳許軍四征有功，必自擇帥；

translations.literal: Early in Taihe, when Zhongwu Military Governor Wang Pei died, public opinion held that because the Chenxu army had fought on four campaigns with achievement it would surely choose its own commander;
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taihe, when Zhongwu Military Governor Wang Pei died, opinion held that because the Chenxu army had fought four campaigns with achievement it would choose its own commander;

sentences.zh: 或以禁軍之將得之。

translations.literal: some thought an imperial guard general would obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: some thought an imperial guard general would get it.

sentences.zh: 宰相裴度、韋處厚議瑀深沈方雅，曾刺陳、蔡，人懷良政，又熟忠武軍情，欲請用瑀。

translations.literal: Chief Ministers Pei Du and Wei Chuhou considered Yu deep, steady, and refined in manner; he had governed Chen and Cai and the people cherished his good governance, and he also knew Zhongwu army sentiment—they wished to recommend Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Ministers Pei Du and Wei Chuhou considered Yu deep, steady, and refined; he had governed Chen and Cai to popular approval and knew Zhongwu army sentiment—they wished to recommend him.

sentences.zh: 事未聞，陳許表至，果請瑀為帥，乃授檢校左散騎常侍、許州刺史、忠武節度使。

translations.literal: Before the matter was heard, a memorial arrived from Chenxu indeed asking that Yu be commander, and he was therefore appointed Supervisory Left Regular Attendant, governor of Xu Prefecture, and military governor of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Before the matter was heard, a Chenxu memorial arrived asking for Yu as commander, and he was appointed supervisory left regular attendant, governor of Xu, and military governor of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 自大歷已來，節制之除拜，多出禁軍中尉。

translations.literal: From the Dalu era onward, appointments as military commissioners mostly came from the inner army supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: From the Dalu era onward, military commissioner appointments mostly came from inner army supervisors.

sentences.zh: 凡命一帥，必廣輸重賂。

translations.literal: Whenever one commander was appointed, heavy bribes had to be paid on a wide scale.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a commander was appointed, heavy bribes had to be paid widely.

sentences.zh: 禁軍將校當為帥者，自無家財，必取資於人；

translations.literal: Imperial guard officers who were to become commanders, having no family wealth, necessarily borrowed from others;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial guard officers slated for command, lacking family wealth, necessarily borrowed from others;

sentences.zh: 得鎮之後，則膏血疲民以償之。

translations.literal: once they obtained command they then drained the people's blood and sweat to repay it.
translations.idiomatic: once in command they drained the people's blood and sweat to repay it.

sentences.zh: 及瑀之拜，以內外公議，搢紳相慶曰：「韋公作相，債帥鮮矣！」

translations.literal: When Yu was appointed, because of consensus inside and outside court, officials congratulated one another, saying: "When Lord Wei became chief minister, debt-commanders became rare!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yu was appointed, with consensus inside and outside court, officials congratulated one another: "When Lord Wei became chief minister, debt-commanders became rare!"

sentences.zh: 三年，就加檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year he was additionally made Supervisory Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was additionally made supervisory minister of works.

sentences.zh: 比年水旱，人民薦饑。

translations.literal: In successive years flood and drought afflicted the people with repeated famine.
translations.idiomatic: In successive years flood and drought brought repeated famine.

sentences.zh: 瑀召集州民，繞郭立堤塘一百八十里，蓄泄既均，人無饑年。

translations.literal: Yu gathered the prefectural people and built embankments and ponds encircling the city for one hundred and eighty li; storage and drainage were balanced, and the people knew no famine year.
translations.idiomatic: Yu gathered prefectural people and built embankments and ponds encircling the city for one hundred and eighty li; storage and drainage were balanced, and the people knew no famine year.

sentences.zh: 加檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Supervisory Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally made supervisory right vice director.

sentences.zh: 六年，移授徐州刺史、武寧軍節度等使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to governor of Xu Prefecture and military governor of the Wu-Ning Army and related posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to governor of Xu and military governor of the Wu-Ning Army and related posts.

sentences.zh: 議者以徐泗王智興之後，軍士驕恣，宜得雄帥鎮之。

translations.literal: Critics said that after Wang Zhixing in Xu and Si the soldiers were arrogant and unrestrained and a fierce commander should be sent to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said that after Wang Zhixing in Xu and Si the soldiers were arrogant and a fierce commander should govern them.

sentences.zh: 乃以太府卿崔珙代瑀，征為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Grand Minister of the Court Cui Gong was therefore made to replace Yu, and Yu was summoned as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister Cui Gong was therefore made to replace Yu, and Yu was summoned as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 以疾求分司，拜太子少傅。

translations.literal: He asked for a separate office on account of illness and was appointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for separate office on account of illness and was appointed junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 其月，復授檢校右僕射、陳許蔡節度使。

translations.literal: That same month he was again appointed Supervisory Right Vice Director and military governor of Chen, Xu, and Cai.
translations.idiomatic: That same month he was again appointed supervisory right vice director and military governor of Chen, Xu, and Cai.

sentences.zh: 八年六月卒，贈司空。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth month of the eighth year and was posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of the eighth year and was posthumously made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 瑀性寬和，有體量，為官雖無赫赫之譽，所至皆理，尤得士心，論者美之。

translations.literal: Yu was mild and generous in nature and had breadth of bearing; though his official service won no resounding praise, everywhere he went was well governed, and he especially won the hearts of scholars—critics praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was mild and generous with breadth of bearing; though his service won no resounding praise, everywhere he went was well governed and he especially won scholars' hearts—critics praised him.

sentences.zh: 崔戎，字可大。

translations.literal: Cui Rong, styled Keda.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Rong, styled Keda.

sentences.zh: 高伯祖玄暐，神龍初有大功，封博陵郡王。

translations.literal: His great-granduncle Xuanwei had great achievement early in Shenlong and was enfeoffed as Prince of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: His great-granduncle Xuanwei had great achievement early in Shenlong and was enfeoffed Prince of Boling.

sentences.zh: 祖嬰，郢州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ying was governor of E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ying was governor of E Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父貞固，太原榆次尉。

translations.literal: His father Zheng'gu was magistrate of Yuci in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zheng'gu was magistrate of Yuci in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 戎舉兩經登科，授太子校書，調判入等，授藍田主薄，為籓鎮名公交辟。

translations.literal: Rong passed both classics examinations, was appointed Crown Prince's Proofreader, was judged superior in evaluation and appointed chief clerk of Lantian, and was repeatedly recruited by famous frontier commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Rong passed both classics examinations, became crown prince's proofreader, was judged superior in evaluation and appointed chief clerk of Lantian, and was repeatedly recruited by famous frontier commanders.

sentences.zh: 裴度領太原，署為參謀。

translations.literal: When Pei Du governed Taiyuan he appointed him as staff planner.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du governed Taiyuan he appointed Rong staff planner.

sentences.zh: 時王承宗據鎮州叛，度請戎單車往諭之，承宗感泣受教。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Chengzong held Zhen Prefecture in rebellion; Du asked Rong to go alone in a single carriage to instruct him, and Chengzong wept and accepted instruction.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chengzong held Zhen Prefecture in rebellion, Du asked Rong to go alone to instruct him, and Chengzong wept and accepted instruction.

sentences.zh: 入為殿中侍御史，累拜吏部郎中，遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He entered court as Palace Censor and was repeatedly promoted to Bureau Director of the Ministry of Personnel and then Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as palace censor, rose to bureau director of personnel, and became censor.

sentences.zh: 尋為劍南東、西兩川宣慰使。

translations.literal: He was soon made pacification commissioner of the Eastern and Western Sichuan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made pacification commissioner of Eastern and Western Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 西州承蠻寇之後，戎既宣撫，兼再定征稅，廢置得所，公私便之。

translations.literal: The western prefectures, having suffered barbarian raids, were both pacified by Rong and had their levies reassessed; abolitions and establishments were appropriate, and public and private alike benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Western prefectures, having suffered barbarian raids, were pacified by Rong; levies were reassessed, abolitions and establishments were appropriate, and public and private alike benefited.

sentences.zh: 還，拜給事中，駁奏為當時所稱。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Drafting Attendant; his memorials of rejection were praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: On return he became drafting attendant; his memorials of rejection were praised at the time.

sentences.zh: 改華州刺史，遷兗海沂密都團練觀察等使。

translations.literal: He was changed to governor of Hua Prefecture and transferred to overall training and surveillance commissioner of Yan, Hai, Yi, and Mi.
translations.idiomatic: He became governor of Hua and overall training and surveillance commissioner of Yan, Hai, Yi, and Mi.

sentences.zh: 將行，州人戀惜遮道，至有解靴斷登者。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, the people, reluctant to part with him, blocked the road; some even pulled off boots and broke carriage steps.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to depart, reluctant people blocked the road; some even pulled off boots and broke carriage steps.

sentences.zh: 理兗一年，大和八年五月卒，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: After governing Yan for one year he died in the fifth month of the eighth year of Dahe and was posthumously granted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After governing Yan one year he died in the fifth month of Dahe 8 and was posthumously made minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 陸亙，字景山，吳郡人。

translations.literal: Lu Gen, styled Jingshan, was a native of Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Gen, styled Jingshan, was from Wu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖元明，睦州司馬。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuanming was vice magistrate of Mu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuanming was vice magistrate of Mu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父持詮，惠陵臺令。

translations.literal: His father Chiquan was magistrate of Huiling Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chiquan was magistrate of Huiling Terrace.

sentences.zh: 亙以書判授集賢殿正字、華原縣尉。

translations.literal: Gen was appointed Proofreader of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and magistrate of Huayuan through document evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Gen was appointed proofreader of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and magistrate of Huayuan through document evaluation.

sentences.zh: 應制舉，授萬年縣丞。

translations.literal: He answered the special examination and was appointed Vice Magistrate of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: He answered the special examination and became vice magistrate of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 自京兆府兵曹參軍拜太常博士。

translations.literal: From Metropolitan Prefecture Army Adjutant he was appointed Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: From metropolitan prefecture army adjutant he became erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 寺有禮生孟真，久於其事，凡吉兇大儀，禮官不能達，率訪真。

translations.literal: In the temple there was ritual attendant Meng Zhen, long in the work; for all great auspicious and inauspicious ceremonies the ritual officers could not master them and always consulted Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the temple was ritual attendant Meng Zhen, long in the work; for all great auspicious and inauspicious ceremonies ritual officers could not master them and always consulted Zhen.

sentences.zh: 真亦賴是須要姑息。

translations.literal: Zhen also relied on this and constantly demanded indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen also relied on this and constantly demanded indulgence.

sentences.zh: 元和七年，冊皇太子，將撰儀註，真亦欲參預；

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanhe, when the crown prince was to be installed and ritual notes were to be drafted, Zhen also wished to participate;
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 7, when the crown prince was to be installed and ritual notes drafted, Zhen also wished to participate;

sentences.zh: 亙笞之，由是禮儀不專於胥吏。

translations.literal: Gen beat him with the staff, and from then on ritual was not monopolized by clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Gen beat him with the staff, and from then on ritual was not monopolized by clerks.

sentences.zh: 自虞部員外郎出為鄧州刺史。

translations.literal: From Assistant in the Ministry of Revenue he was sent out as governor of Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: From assistant in the Ministry of Revenue he was sent out as governor of Deng.

sentences.zh: 其後入為戶部郎中、秘書少監、太常少卿，歷刺兗、蔡、虢、蘇四郡。

translations.literal: He later entered court as Bureau Director of the Ministry of Revenue, Junior Director of the Secretariat, Junior Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, and governed Yan, Cai, Guo, and Su prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He later entered court as revenue bureau director, junior director of the secretariat, junior minister of imperial sacrifices, and governed Yan, Cai, Guo, and Su.

sentences.zh: 遷越州刺史、浙東團練觀察等使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor of Yue Prefecture and overall training and surveillance commissioner of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Yue and overall training and surveillance commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 移宣歙觀察使，加御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was moved to surveillance commissioner of Xuan and She and additionally made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to surveillance commissioner of Xuan and She and additionally made censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 太和八年九月卒，年七十一，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died in the ninth month of the eighth year of Taihe at the age of seventy-one and was posthumously granted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of Taihe 8, aged seventy-one, and was posthumously made minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 亙強明嚴毅，所至稱理。

translations.literal: Gen was forceful, bright, strict, and resolute; everywhere he went was praised as well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Gen was forceful, bright, strict, and resolute; everywhere he went was praised as well governed.

sentences.zh: 初赴兗州，延英面奏曰：「凡節度使握兵分屯屬郡者，刺史不能制，遂為一州之弊，宜有處分。」

translations.literal: When he first went to Yan Prefecture he addressed the emperor at Yanying and said: "Whenever military governors hold troops garrisoned in subordinate prefectures, the prefect cannot control them, and this becomes a prefecture's affliction—there should be disposition."
translations.idiomatic: When he first went to Yan he addressed the emperor at Yanying: "Whenever military governors hold troops garrisoned in subordinate prefectures, prefects cannot control them, and this becomes a prefecture's affliction—there should be disposition."

sentences.zh: 因詔天下兵分屯屬郡者，隸於刺史。

translations.literal: An edict therefore ordered that troops garrisoned in subordinate prefectures throughout the realm be placed under prefects.
translations.idiomatic: An edict therefore ordered troops garrisoned in subordinate prefectures throughout the realm placed under prefects.

sentences.zh: 越之永喜郡，城於海閆，常陷寇境，集官吏廩祿之半，以代常賦，因循相踵，吏返為幸。

translations.literal: In Yongjia command of Yue a city was built on the seashore, often falling within raider territory; officials and clerks had half their salaries and grain stores collected to replace regular levies; this continued by inertia and clerks came to regard it as good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongjia command of Yue a seashore city often fell within raider territory; officials and clerks had half their salaries and grain stores collected to replace regular levies; this continued by inertia and clerks came to regard it as fortune.

sentences.zh: 亙按舉贓罪，表請郡守以降，增給其俸，人皆賴之。

translations.literal: Gen investigated corruption offenses, memorialized that prefects and below should have their salaries increased, and the people all relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Gen investigated corruption, memorialized that prefects and below should have salaries increased, and the people all relied on him.

sentences.zh: 張正甫，字踐方，南陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhengfu, styled Jianfang, was a native of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhengfu, styled Jianfang, was from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖大禮，坊州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Dali was governor of Fang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Dali was governor of Fang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖紹貞，尚書右丞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shaozhen was Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shaozhen was right vice director.

sentences.zh: 父泚，蘇州司馬。

translations.literal: His father Ci was vice magistrate of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ci was vice magistrate of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 正甫登進士第，從樊澤為襄陽從事，累轉監察御史。

translations.literal: Zhengfu passed the jinshi examination, followed Fan Ze as staff in Xiangyang, and was repeatedly promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengfu passed the jinshi examination, followed Fan Ze as staff in Xiangyang, and rose to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 於頔代澤，辟留正甫。

translations.literal: When Yu Di replaced Ze he recruited and retained Zhengfu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Di replaced Ze he recruited and retained Zhengfu.

sentences.zh: 正甫堅辭之，遂誣奏貶郴州長史。

translations.literal: Zhengfu firmly declined and was therefore falsely reported and demoted to Long Chief of Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengfu firmly declined and was falsely reported and demoted to long chief of Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後由邕府征拜殿中侍御史，遷戶部員外郎，轉司封員外、兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned from Yong prefecture staff as Palace Censor, promoted to Assistant in the Ministry of Revenue, and transferred to Assistant in the Bureau of Honors and concurrently Investigating Censor with charge of miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later summoned from Yong staff as palace censor, he rose to assistant in the Ministry of Revenue and assistant in the Bureau of Honors with concurrent charge of investigating censor and miscellaneous affairs.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部郎中，改河南尹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Bureau Director of the Ministry of Revenue and changed to metropolitan governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to revenue bureau director and became metropolitan governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 由尚書右丞為同州刺史，入拜左散騎常侍、集賢殿學士判院事。

translations.literal: From Right Vice Director he became governor of Tong Prefecture; he entered court as Left Regular Attendant and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with charge of the academy.
translations.idiomatic: From right vice director he became governor of Tong; he entered court as left regular attendant and academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with charge of the academy.

sentences.zh: 轉工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 五年，檢校兵部尚書、太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made Supervisory Minister of War and Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made supervisory minister of war and mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 明年，以吏部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: The next year he retired as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he retired as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 正甫仁而端亮，蒞官清強。

translations.literal: Zhengfu was benevolent, upright, and bright; in office he was clear and forceful.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengfu was benevolent, upright, and bright; in office he was clear and forceful.

sentences.zh: 居外任，所至稱理。

translations.literal: In outer appointments everywhere he went was praised as well governed.
translations.idiomatic: In outer appointments everywhere he went was praised as well governed.

sentences.zh: 太和八年九月卒，年八十三，累贈太師。

translations.literal: He died in the ninth month of the eighth year of Taihe at the age of eighty-three and was repeatedly posthumously granted Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of Taihe 8, aged eighty-three, and was repeatedly posthumously made grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 子毅夫。

translations.literal: His son was Yifu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yifu.

sentences.zh: 毅夫，登進士第。

translations.literal: Yifu passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 初正甫兄式，大歷中進士登第，繼之以正甫，式子元夫、傑夫、征夫又相次登科。

translations.literal: At first Zhengfu's elder brother Shi passed the jinshi in the Dalu era, followed by Zhengfu; Shi's sons Yuanfu, Jiefu, and Zhengfu in turn passed the examination in succession.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhengfu's elder brother Shi passed the jinshi in the Dalu era, followed by Zhengfu; Shi's sons Yuanfu, Jiefu, and Zhengfu passed in succession.

sentences.zh: 太和中，文章之盛，世共稱之。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era the flourishing of literary talent was praised together by the age.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era the flourishing of literary talent was praised by the age.

sentences.zh: 元夫，太和初兵部郎中、知制誥，遷中書舍人，出為汝州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuanfu, early in Taihe, was Bureau Director of the Ministry of War and drafting drafter, was promoted to Drafting Attendant, and was sent out as governor of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu, early in Taihe, was war bureau director and drafting drafter, rose to drafting attendant, and was sent out as governor of Ru.

sentences.zh: 毅夫位至戶部侍郎、弘文館學士判院事。

translations.literal: Yifu rose to Vice Minister of Revenue and academician of the Hongwen Hall with charge of the academy.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu rose to vice minister of revenue and Hongwen Hall academician with charge of the academy.

sentences.zh: 諸群從登第者數人，而毅夫子祎最知名。

translations.literal: Several cousins passed the examination; among them Yifu's son Yi was most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Several cousins passed the examination; among them Yifu's son Yi was most renowned.

sentences.zh: 祎，字冠章，釋褐汴州從事、戶部判官，入為藍田尉、集賢校理。

translations.literal: Yi, styled Guanzhang, on leaving office served as staff in Bian Prefecture and revenue judge, entered court as magistrate of Lantian and collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Guanzhang, first served as staff in Bian and revenue judge, entered court as magistrate of Lantian and collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 趙隱鎮浙西，劉鄴鎮淮南，皆辟為賓佐。

translations.literal: When Zhao Yin governed Zhexi and Liu Ye governed Huainan, both recruited him as staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Yin governed Zhexi and Liu Ye governed Huainan, both recruited him as staff.

sentences.zh: 入為監察御史，遷左補闕。

translations.literal: He entered court as Investigating Censor and was promoted to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as investigating censor and rose to left reminder.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，詔入翰林為學士，累官至中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the Qianfu era an edict summoned him to the Hanlin Academy as academician; he rose repeatedly to Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianfu era an edict summoned him to the Hanlin Academy; he rose repeatedly to drafting attendant.

sentences.zh: 黃巢犯京師，從僖宗幸蜀，拜工部侍郎，判戶部事。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao attacked the capital he followed Emperor Xizong to Shu and was appointed Vice Minister of Works with charge of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao attacked the capital he followed Emperor Xizong to Shu and was appointed vice minister of works with charge of revenue.

sentences.zh: 奉使江淮還，為當塗者不協，改太子賓客、左散騎常侍，轉吏部侍郎，歷刑部、兵部尚書。

translations.literal: On returning from a mission to the Jianghuai region he was at odds with the man in power and was changed to Crown Prince's Mentor and Left Regular Attendant, then Vice Minister of Personnel, and successively Minister of Justice and Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from a Jianghuai mission he was at odds with the man in power and was changed to crown prince's mentor and left regular attendant, then vice minister of personnel, and successively minister of justice and minister of war.

sentences.zh: 從昭宗在華，為韓建所構，貶衡州司馬。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Zhaozong at Hua he was framed by Han Jian and demoted to Vice Magistrate of Heng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Following Emperor Zhaozong at Hua he was framed by Han Jian and demoted to vice magistrate of Heng.

sentences.zh: 昭宗還京，征拜禮部尚書、太常卿，充禮儀使，遷兵部尚書。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong returned to the capital he was summoned as Minister of Rites and Grand Minister of Imperial Sacrifices and made ritual commissioner, then promoted to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong returned to the capital he was summoned as minister of rites and grand minister of imperial sacrifices and ritual commissioner, then promoted to minister of war.

sentences.zh: 祎苦心為文，老而益壯。

translations.literal: Yi labored at writing; in old age his work grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Yi labored at writing; in old age his work grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 為刑部時，劉鄴子覃，當巢寇時避禍於金吾將軍張直方之第，被害。

translations.literal: When he was Minister of Justice, Liu Ye's son Tan, during the Huang Chao rebellion, had taken refuge in the residence of Gold Crow Guard commander Zhang Zhifang and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When he was minister of justice, Liu Ye's son Tan, during the Huang Chao rebellion, had taken refuge in Gold Crow Guard commander Zhang Zhifang's residence and was killed.

sentences.zh: 僖宗還京，而惡覃者以托附逆黨，死不以義，下三司詳罪。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong returned to the capital those who hated Tan accused him of attaching himself to the rebel party and dying without righteousness; the Three Offices were ordered to examine the crime in detail.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong returned to the capital those who hated Tan accused him of attaching himself to rebels and dying without righteousness; the Three Offices were ordered to examine the crime.

sentences.zh: 祎上章申理，言覃父子並命於賊廷，豈附逆耶？

translations.literal: Yi submitted a memorial in his defense, saying father and son both met their deaths in the rebel court—how could this be joining rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: Yi submitted a memorial in his defense, saying father and son both met death in the rebel court—how could this be joining rebellion?

sentences.zh: 其家竟獲洗雪，覃亦贈官。

translations.literal: His family finally obtained rehabilitation and Tan was also posthumously granted office.
translations.idiomatic: His family finally obtained rehabilitation and Tan was also posthumously granted office.

sentences.zh: 其行義始終，皆如此類。

translations.literal: His righteous conduct from beginning to end was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His righteous conduct from beginning to end was all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：孟陽、王遂儒雅之曹，才有可稱，竟以財媚時君，陷為俗吏。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Mengyang and Wang Sui were men of refined learning; their talent was praiseworthy, yet they finally used wealth to flatter the ruler of the time and fell into being vulgar officials.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Mengyang and Wang Sui were men of refined learning with praiseworthy talent, yet they finally used wealth to flatter the ruler and fell into being vulgar officials.

sentences.zh: 蹈道之論，可不懼耶！

translations.literal: The discourse on treading the Way—should one not fear it?
translations.idiomatic: The discourse on treading the Way—should one not fear it?

sentences.zh: 全義官由妄進，霞寓位以卒升，勇毅不足以啟行，謀慮不足以應變，敗亡之辱，不亦宜乎？

translations.literal: Quanyi's office came from reckless advancement; Xiayi's rank rose from the ranks; courage and resolution were insufficient to open the way, and planning was insufficient to meet change—the shame of defeat and ruin was not it fitting?
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi's office came from reckless advancement; Xiayi's rank rose from the ranks; courage was insufficient to open the way and planning insufficient to meet change—the shame of defeat was not fitting?

sentences.zh: 朝無責帥之刑，蓋自恥也。

translations.literal: The court had no punishment for commanders who failed; this was rather its own shame.
translations.idiomatic: The court had no punishment for failed commanders; this was rather its own shame.

sentences.zh: 權、瑀長者，末塗喪真，雖牽於食貧，純則偽矣。

translations.literal: Quan and Yu were elder men; in their final years they lost their integrity—though dragged by poverty for food, if pure it was false.
translations.idiomatic: Quan and Yu were elder men; in their final years they lost integrity—though dragged by poverty, if pure it was false.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：蘊仁則哲，蘊利則狂。

translations.literal: The encomium says: To store benevolence is wisdom; to store profit is madness.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: To store benevolence is wisdom; to store profit is madness.

sentences.zh: 搢紳之胤，勿效潘、王。

translations.literal: Descendants of the gentry—do not imitate Pan and Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants of the gentry—do not imitate Pan and Wang.

sentences.zh: 全義逃責，貞元失策。

translations.literal: Quanyi escaped responsibility; Zhenyuan lost its way.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi escaped responsibility; Zhenyuan lost its way.

sentences.zh: 霞寓薄刑，元和復興。

translations.literal: Xiayi received light punishment; Yuanhe revived.
translations.idiomatic: Xiayi received light punishment; Yuanhe revived.
